extracted.intended_audience: Researchers applying to JSPS KAKENHI and peer reviewers (researchers assessing KAKENHI proposals)
extracted.subtask_description: Official review criteria and process used by the Japan Society for the Promotion of Science (JSPS) to evaluate KAKENHI research proposals; describes evaluation items, scoring, reviewer composition, and procedural stages (including special two-stage review for larger grants).

rubrics_metrics.name: Research Subject
rubrics_metrics.description: Originality and creativity; Importance and relevance; Significance of contributions; Position relative to international research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether the research topic is novel and creative, addresses an important/relevant question, will make significant contributions, and how the project is positioned compared with international research in the field.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research Method
rubrics_metrics.description: Validity of research plan; Feasibility; Achievability within funding period; Logical structure of research approach.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether the proposed methods are valid and logically structured, whether the plan is feasible and achievable within the grant period, and whether the approach can realistically produce the claimed outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research Capability
rubrics_metrics.description: Track record; Research environment; Necessary equipment, samples, expertise; Track record of research execution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge the principal investigator(s) and team based on past performance and ability to execute the project, and assess whether the institutional environment, equipment, samples, and expertise needed are available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research Funding (Budget Reasonableness)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reasonableness of requested budget; Necessity of expenses; Cost-benefit reasonableness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examine whether requested expenses are necessary and reasonable for the proposed work, and whether the costs are justified given the expected benefits and outputs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review Method (peer review by related-field researchers)
rubrics_metrics.description: Diverse academic research based on researchers' free ideas is reviewed through peer review by researchers in related fields; review conducted in accordance with the Review Section Table and revised Review Method.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviews are performed by experts in related fields following JSPS's Review Section Table and revised procedures; reviewers assess proposals as peers rather than against preset topical priorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Two-Stage Review (for some categories/larger grants)
rubrics_metrics.description: Stage 1: Document review by 5-6 reviewers. Stage 2: Panel discussion and selection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For larger grants, initial scoring is done by multiple external reviewers (typically 5–6) and top-ranked proposals are then discussed in a panel for final selection; procedural expectation affects how proposals should be written for both document-only and panel scrutiny.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer Pool Expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: Approximately 8,000 reviewers selected from each academic field; prominent researchers who work hard at each academic field; stand at the front of knowledge creation; review and assess applications for their peers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Know that reviewers are senior/active researchers across fields; proposals will be assessed by peers with high subject-matter expectations — clarity, rigor, and demonstrated capability are essential.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation Scale and Weighting
rubrics_metrics.description: Generally uses a 4-point or 5-point scale; weighted across the four evaluation items; final ranking determines funding within available budget.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scoring typically uses a 4- or 5-point numeric scale applied to the four main evaluation items (Research Subject, Research Method, Research Capability, Research Funding); scores are weighted to produce a final ranking that determines funding allocation given budget constraints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program Features: free-form research and topical openness
rubrics_metrics.description: Free-form research (researchers propose their own ideas); no predetermined topical priorities (unlike strategic programs); continuous funding model with multi-year grants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: KAKENHI emphasizes investigator-initiated, curiosity-driven research rather than adherence to preset strategic themes; proposals should foreground original ideas and long-term scholarly contribution rather than fitting a topical priority call.
